subject: english-literature
title: Like, As, Is
welcome_lead: Two tiny words turn comparison into magic. Learn the difference.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on similes vs metaphors.
final_note: You can now tell similes from metaphors at a glance.

concepts.def: Showing one thing in terms of another.
The image used to describe the subject.
Pictures created in the reader's mind.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Her eyes were like stars' is a simile. 'As cold as ice' is a simile. The little word does the work.
'Her eyes were stars' is a metaphor. No 'like'/'as' — just the bold claim that one thing IS another.
In 'time is a thief', the tenor is time, the vehicle is a thief. The vehicle delivers the picture.

mcqs.q: 'As brave as a lion' is a.
'The classroom was a zoo' is a.

numericals.q: How many little words make a simile (like, as)?

free_texts.q: A comparison using 'like' or 'as' is a ____.
